thread:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — thanks for the reviews. We need to lock a pragmatic SDK surface for Python/TS/Go that keeps transports tiny and portable. My proposal: minimal Transport interface + explicit paginator adapters, and retries as a small orthogonal policy object. Thoughts?

mika: +1 to tiny transport. We should avoid coupling pagination into transport. Lots of backend paging models (cursor, offset, streaming).

jamie: Agreed. For ergonomics we should provide two high-level iterators: SyncPaginator (for py/ts sync) and AsyncPaginator (async/streams). Transport only needs unary and streaming hooks.

priya: quick sketch of transport shape I had in mind:
```ts
// minimal, crosslang-friendly
interface Transport {
  unary(req: Request): Promise<Response>
  stream?(req: Request): AsyncIterable<Buffer> // optional, for streaming routes
}
```
kevin: That looks fine. Key tradeoff: do we let transport return partial pages (server-driven) or always coerce to a uniform Page shape? I prefer letting paginator own normalization.

mika: +1 — keep normalization out of transport so we can support weird backends w/o changing transport impls.

alex: Retry policy: make it pluggable and idempotency-aware. Default: exponential backoff with jitter, max 5 retries for idempotent unary. Streaming/long-poll shouldn't retry automatically.

jamie: Edge case: paginated list where nextPageToken request is non-idempotent (rare). We should provide an explicit per-call flag and a helper that marks a call as safe-to-retry when prompt/params are deterministic.

priya: Proposal for SDK call helper signature (keeps surface tiny):
```py
call = client.call(route, params, *, retry_policy=None, idempotent=True, paginator=None)
# paginator is optional adapter class
```
kevin: Love explicit flags. For TS/Go we can mirror that pattern: options bag. Default idempotent=true could be dangerous. Maybe default to auto-detect for known list routes, otherwise false?

alex: Good point. Let's default to false and provide a lightweight detection map for known list/read endpoints in our model catalog and docs. Safer.

mika: Pagination ergonomics: provide two helpers — `pages()` that yields raw page objects (token, items) and `items()` that yields flattened items. Keep both so apps can choose.

jamie: Streaming vs pagination: For large single resource streams (transcript, logs) prefer a stream API. For paginated list endpoints keep streaming optional but supported by transport.

priya: Implementation notes: keep transport layer free of SDK-specific types. Use plain JSON-ish Request/Response and let language-specific adapters wrap into nicer objects. That avoids crosslang churn.

kevin: Backoff defaults: initial=100ms, multiplier=2, max_delay=5s, max_retries=4 (for idempotent unary). We can tune later. Add a debug header when retry happens for observability.

alex: Owners/timeline:
- opt surface design + doc: @alex (this thread) by EOW
- implement transport adapter shim in TS/Python: @jamie + @mika next sprint
- retry policy lib and defaults: @kevin prototype by mid next sprint
- change lists to default idempotent=false and publish migration guide: @priya

ops-bot: deploy-bot: New RFC note added to docs/RFCs: "crosslang transport: slim api + explicit paginator" (link: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/xxxxx) :white_check_mark:

mika: one more thing — keep an escape hatch: advanced users can register a custom paginator/transport pair. Should be easy to plugin.

alex: Agree. OK — unless objections, I'll draft the follow-up doc capturing these decisions and the API sketches above. If no strong objections by EOD I'll mark this resolved and start PRs. :thumbsup:

priya: no objections from me. thanks all.

kevin: fine by me. small nit: include an example of migrating existing clients from current paginated helpers to `pages()`/`items()` in the doc.

jamie: noted, will add example snippets for py/ts.

alex: thanks — closing soon if quiet.
